assertions.text: Output contains at least 2 separate markdown tables (not everything crammed into one table)
assertions.evidence: Three distinct tables are presented: Table 1 (Cancellation Refund Eligibility), Table 2 (Prorated Refund Amount), and Table 3 (Free Trial Lifecycle)

assertions.text: The tables cover distinct concerns — e.g. pricing/plans is separate from cancellation/refund rules
assertions.evidence: Table 1 covers refund eligibility decisions, Table 2 covers refund amount calculations, Table 3 covers trial lifecycle events—each addresses a distinct business concern

assertions.text: At least one output column in each table ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: Table 1 has 'Refund Eligible?' and 'Reason?'; Table 2 has 'Refund Amount?'; Table 3 has 'Subscription Status After?' and 'Charge Taken?'

assertions.text: The 24-hour no-refund exception is included as a distinct scenario row
assertions.evidence: Table 1 Row 2: 'Cancel within 24h of renewal' with 'Refund Eligible?: no' and 'Reason?: Within no-refund window'; Row 6 explicitly tests the 24h boundary

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — no implementation terms like 'boolean', 'int', 'isProrated', camelCase identifiers
assertions.evidence: All column headers use business language: 'Refund Eligible?', 'Plan Type', 'Subscription Status', 'Cycle Length (Policy)', 'Days Remaining', 'Charge Taken?', 'Subscription Status After?'—no technical identifiers present

assertions.text: Includes a row or scenario for cancelling during the free trial — no charge was made, so no refund applies. This case should be explicit, not omitted.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 Row 1: 'Cancel during free trial' with 'Refund Eligible?: no' and 'Reason?: No charge taken yet'; Table 3 Row 1 also covers 'Subscriber cancels mid-trial'

assertions.text: The prorated refund calculation is shown or explained — e.g. days remaining × daily rate, or an equivalent formula. Not just 'prorated refund' without showing how.
assertions.evidence: Explicit formula provided: 'Refund = Plan Cost × Days Remaining ÷ Cycle Length, floored to the nearest penny'

assertions.text: The 24-hour no-refund window is tested near the boundary (e.g. values at or close to 23h, 24h, 25h) — not just 'within 24h' vs 'well after renewal'.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 includes Row 3 'Cancel just outside 24h, monthly', Row 4 'Cancel just outside 24h, annual', and Row 6 'Cancel at exactly 24h after renewal'—testing at, just inside, and just outside the boundary

assertions.text: Refund eligibility (yes/no, based on 24h rule and trial status) and refund amount (prorated calculation) are in separate tables — not mixed into one table. This separation makes each concern independently reviewable.
assertions.evidence: Table 1 covers eligibility with 'Refund Eligible?' column; Table 2 covers amount with 'Refund Amount?' column—separate tables as required

assertions.text: The '?' suffix is only used on output/expected columns (e.g. 'Refund Eligible?', 'Refund Amount?') — not on input columns like plan type, loyalty status, or yes/no flags. Input columns should not have '?' suffixes.
assertions.evidence: Input columns ('Plan Type', 'Subscription Status', 'Days Since Trial Start', 'Event', 'Cycle Length (Policy)', 'Days Remaining') lack '?' suffixes; '?' appears only on output columns ('Refund Eligible?', 'Reason?', 'Refund Amount?', 'Subscription Status After?', 'Charge Taken?')
